items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: she always told him, “Why can’t you be more like Nat Cole?” He couldn’t stand that. Nathaniel.

ctx.x: I think it was his mother, yeah.

Milt had a difficult relationship with his mother. It was different. Of course she exerted a great influence on him too, she was a music teacher. But she was always disappointed in him she wanted him to play piano, he wanted to play violin, and so she always told him, “Why can’t you be more like Nat Cole?” He couldn’t stand that. Nathaniel. “Why can’t you be more like Nathaniel?” But Joe didn’t have that difficulty with his mother, not at all. But yes, they all came from the south and those who succeeded did have…

Well speaking about, “Why can’t you be like Nat Cole,” I read a few things about when Joe had to replace, when Joe became Basie’s singer, he had to follow Jimmy Rushing, and apparently there was some problems with that I guess, maybe over in England or something.
